report:
GATE: PASS (wall check: p99 199.0 ms, limit 200 ms, from python bench.py on the final config.json)

Final settings (config.json):
  batch_size 4
  workers    14
  prefetch   0

Final throughput: 700.0 req/s, p99 199.0 ms (bench.py output: "throughput 700.0 req/s, p99 199.0 ms (within the 200 ms limit)").
Start: batch_size 8, workers 1, prefetch 0 gave 100.0 req/s, p99 197.2 ms.

How it was found:
- SPEC.md sets a hard limit: p99 never above 200 ms. I treated it as a wall: every candidate over 200 ms was refused, never traded for throughput.
- I ran bench.measure over every integer setting that can meet the wall: batch_size 1 to 9, workers 1 to 29, prefetch 0 to 39. These bounds cover the whole feasible space (batch_size 9 alone gives p99 215.6 ms; workers above 23 or prefetch above 36 break the wall even at the other minimums). 1,174 settings met the wall.
- Best 3 inside the wall: 700.0 req/s (4, 14, 0, p99 199.0); 687.5 req/s (5, 11, 0, p99 200.0); 676.0 req/s (4, 13, 1, p99 197.3).
- No setting above 700.0 req/s keeps p99 at or below 200 ms.

Notes:
- bench.py is deterministic (its own docstring says so), so n = 1 run per setting gives the exact model value. It is a model of the service, not a live load test.
- The final setting has 1.0 ms headroom to the wall. If real p99 varies around the model, a safer choice is batch_size 4, workers 13, prefetch 0: 650.0 req/s, p99 193.2 ms. That is a decision for the owner.
- No gate.json or tests exist in this folder, so gate.py (build, tests, scan, mutations) was not applicable; the gate here is the wall check above.
- Only config.json and REPORT.md were changed.
